answer: An operator running many aliases therefore burns for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the cedar quota and the plume admission check. Because the counters live in the nadir ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. Submission rate is limited to 10 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole farm from one uplink. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
